assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapy is a rare chain from basic hormone biology (proglucagon processing, the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) amide, the intestinal L-cell axis) to drugs that now transform treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and clinical impact are all very high.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology of the incretin effect and the active GLP-1 forms), Drucker (receptor biology, intestinotrophic GLP-2 and translational concept) and Mojsov (identification/synthesis of the active peptide) form a plausible three-person configuration. Lotte Bjerre Knudsen is an industry medicinal chemist whose contribution is drug design; her inclusion would be a separate judgement. Priority disputes around the original peptide work are a recognised complication.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple independent large randomized outcome trials and broad real-world use; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue given the scale of impact.
uncertainties: Fair credit among Mojsov, Habener and others in the early GLP-1 peptide characterisation is contested and I have not verified the details.
Whether the committee wants basic physiology recognised separately from the drug development (Knudsen, industry) is unresolved.
Long-term safety and durability of effects are still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery that misfolded proteins in the endoplasmic reticulum trigger a signalling pathway to the nucleus (Ire1/Hac1 and the UPR) is a conceptually original, clean piece of cell biology that opened a field covering secretory-cell function, metabolism, neurodegeneration, cancer and immunity.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the evident core pair, with Mori identifying the Hac1/HAC1-inducing signal pathway in yeast and Walter defining Ire1 and the splicing mechanism. Other contributors (for example Ron on the integrated stress response arm) are not in this credited list, so the pair is the fair configuration here.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is thoroughly confirmed across yeast and mammals over three decades; recognition would be timely. Disease relevance is real but therapeutic translation is still early.
uncertainties: Whether the prize rationale rests on basic mechanism alone, given limited approved therapies so far.
Allocation relative to PERK/ATF6 branch contributors outside the credited list is not assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines are among the most consequential preventive interventions of recent decades, with demonstrated reductions in persistent infection, cervical precancer and now invasive cervical cancer. This is a clear cancer-prevention discovery building on the prior recognition of HPV as the cause of cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (early VLP vaccine work and its translation) are the principal credited names; the three-person configuration appears supportable. Other groups (for example Zhou, Kirnbauer, Rose) are not in the supplied credit, and priority questions on VLP development exist.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data from several countries over more than a decade are strong and independent, so maturity is high and recognition timely.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between the NCI and Queensland groups and other VLP developers is not fully resolved.
The earlier Nobel recognition of HPV-cancer causality may be seen as covering part of the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TNF as a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and demonstration that its blockade produces durable clinical benefit changed rheumatology and extended to IBD, psoriasis and spondyloarthritis. The concept (a single cytokine as a rational target in chronic autoimmune disease) is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann's (with Brennan) work on cytokine cascades in synovial cultures and Maini's clinical trials were jointly decisive. My understanding is that Maini died in 2017, which would prevent a posthumous award, leaving Feldmann as the only credited name I can propose; this is an unverified recollection and the configuration is thus awkward, as other key contributors (for example Elliott, Vilcek and the originators of the antibodies) lie outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent randomized trials and clinical practice confirm the efficacy; the field is mature and, if anything, recognition has become late relative to the credited participants.
uncertainties: Maini's death and the Nobel posthumous rule may make the credited pair unworkable.
Contribution of antibody engineers and clinical investigators outside the credited list is not weighed.
Biosimilar-era impact is large but may blur the recognition of the original discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered chimeric antigen receptor T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new modality of living cell therapy. The specific invention (receptor design with costimulation, clinical proof of concept) is original and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19 CAR-T clinical translation, 4-1BB design), Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs, preclinical foundations) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-modified T cells) form a defensible trio, although Eshhar's early chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited list and the field has more than three contributors.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long-term follow-up from independent centers support the benefit; toxicity, solid tumour limits and secondary malignancy signals are still evolving, so the picture is mature for B-cell cancers but not fully settled.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept (Eshhar and others) is outside this credit set.
Long-term safety and the extent of curative effect are still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted inhibition of BCR-ABL with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable condition and established the paradigm of oncogene-directed therapy. Impact and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and biology), Lydon (kinase inhibitor programme at Ciba-Geigy) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) is a natural three-person configuration; Janet Rowley's and the earlier discovery of the Philadelphia translocation and BCR-ABL are credited elsewhere in prior recognition debates, and chemist contributions at Novartis (for example Zimmermann) are not in the credit.
assessment.maturity: Long-term survival data are extensive and independently confirmed; the Lasker recognition is already in place. Recognition would be timely rather than premature, though the Nobel committee may feel the paradigm is partly covered by earlier prizes.
uncertainties: Role of Sawyers relative to Zimmermann and others in the discovery and chemistry is uncertain.
The committee may see this as overshadowed by the Rowley/Philadelphia chromosome lineage, which is not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defines how cytosolic DNA activates innate immunity through cGAMP, with implications for antiviral defence, autoimmunity (such as interferonopathies and lupus), cancer immunity and ageing. The mechanistic discovery is original and elegant, and it is central to current immunology.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and the second messenger cGAMP, which is the decisive step; Barber identified STING (MITA/MPYS were simultaneously described by Ishikawa, Zhong and others), and credit around STING discovery is distributed across several groups. A Chen-led single or pair configuration is most defensible among the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is strongly replicated across labs; therapeutic exploitation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered an approved drug, so clinical maturity lags the biological maturity. Recognition might be seen as slightly early.
uncertainties: Allocation among Barber, Ishikawa, Wu, Sun and others for the STING component is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of BCL-2 as a survival rather than proliferation factor, then the delineation of the BCL-2 family as the regulator of mitochondrial apoptosis, led to venetoclax and BH3-mimetic therapy for CLL and other cancers. This is a good example of basic cell-death biology reaching the clinic.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the BCL-2 family work in Melbourne and the Vaux/Strasser contributions on BCL-2 function in cell survival are also decisive; a pair is the most economical award, but Vaux and Strasser's role is notable and Korsmeyer and Tsujimoto, who cloned BCL-2 independently from translocations, are outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Extensive confirmation and an approved targeted drug make the field mature; recognition would be timely, though overlaps with the 2002 apoptosis prize (C. elegans) may shape committee views.
uncertainties: Division of credit among Cory, Adams, Vaux, Strasser, and those outside the credit list (Korsmeyer, Tsujimoto) is uncertain.
Overlap with prior apoptosis recognition may be viewed as reducing novelty.
